DisplayNameForForm: Activities of Daily Living (ADL) Assistance. Self-Performance
CodingInstructions: Code for resident's performance over all shifts - not including setup. If the ADL activity occurred 3 or more times at various levels of assistance, code the most dependent - except for total dependence, which requires full staff performance every time Refer to the ADL flow chart in the RAI manual to facilitate accurate coding.   Instructions for Rule of 3: When an activity occurs three times at any one given level, code that level. When an activity occurs three times at multiple levels, code the most dependent, exceptions are total dependence (4), activity must require full assist every time, and activity did not occur (8), activity must not have occurred at all. Example, three times extensive assistance (3) and three times limited assistance (2), code extensive assistance (3). When an activity occurs at various levels, but not three times at any given level, apply the following:  When there is a combination of full staff performance, and extensive assistance, code extensive assistance. When there is a combination of full staff performance, weight bearing assistance and/or non-weight bearing assistance code limited assistance (2). If none of the above are met, code supervision

Example, three times extensive assistance (3) and three times limited assistance (2), code extensive assistance (3). When an activity occurs at various levels, but not three times at any given level, apply the following:  When there is a combination of full staff performance, and extensive assistance, code extensive assistance. When there is a combination of full staff performance, weight bearing assistance and/or non-weight bearing assistance code limited assistance (2). If none of the above are met, code supervision

DisplayNameForForm: Activities of Daily Living (ADL) Assistance. Self-Performance
CodingInstructions: Code for resident's performance over all shifts - not including setup. If the ADL activity occurred 3 or more times at various levels of assistance, code the most dependent - except for total dependence, which requires full staff performance every time Refer to the ADL flow chart in the RAI manual to facilitate accurate coding.   Instructions for Rule of 3: When an activity occurs three times at any one given level, code that level. When an activity occurs three times at multiple levels, code the most dependent, exceptions are total dependence (4), activity must require full assist every time, and activity did not occur (8), activity must not have occurred at all. Example, three times extensive assistance (3) and three times limited assistance (2), code extensive assistance (3). When an activity occurs at various levels, but not three times at any given level, apply the following:  When there is a combination of full staff performance, and extensive assistance, code extensive assistance. When there is a combination of full staff performance, weight bearing assistance and/or non-weight bearing assistance code limited assistance (2). If none of the above are met, code supervision

LoincName: MDS v3.0 - RAI v1.17.2 - Activities of daily living (ADL) assistance - self-performance - OSA:-:RptPeriod:^Patient:-:CMS Assessment
DisplayNameForForm: Activities of Daily Living (ADL) Assistance. Self-Performance
CodingInstructions: Code for resident's performance over all shifts - not including setup. If the ADL activity occurred 3 or more times at various levels of assistance, code the most dependent - except for total dependence, which requires full staff performance every time Refer to the ADL flow chart in the RAI manual to facilitate accurate coding.   Instructions for Rule of 3: When an activity occurs three times at any one given level, code that level. When an activity occurs three times at multiple levels, code the most dependent, exceptions are total dependence (4), activity must require full assist every time, and activity did not occur (8), activity must not have occurred at all. Example, three times extensive assistance (3) and three times limited assistance (2), code extensive assistance (3). When an activity occurs at various levels, but not three times at any given level, apply the following:  When there is a combination of full staff performance, and extensive assistance, code extensive assistance. When there is a combination of full staff performance, weight bearing assistance and/or non-weight bearing assistance code limited assistance (2). If none of the above are met, code supervision

LoincName: MDS v3.0 - RAI v1.17.2 - Activities of daily living (ADL) assistance - self-performance:-:RptPeriod:^Patient:-:CMS Assessment
DisplayNameForForm: Activities of Daily Living (ADL) Assistance. Self-Performance
CodingInstructions: Code for resident's performance over all shifts - not including setup. If the ADL activity occurred 3 or more times at various levels of assistance, code the most dependent - except for total dependence, which requires full staff performance every time Refer to the ADL flow chart in the RAI manual to facilitate accurate coding.   Instructions for Rule of 3: When an activity occurs three times at any one given level, code that level. When an activity occurs three times at multiple levels, code the most dependent, exceptions are total dependence (4), activity must require full assist every time, and activity did not occur (8), activity must not have occurred at all. Example, three times extensive assistance (3) and three times limited assistance (2), code extensive assistance (3). When an activity occurs at various levels, but not three times at any given level, apply the following:  When there is a combination of full staff performance, and extensive assistance, code extensive assistance. When there is a combination of full staff performance, weight bearing assistance and/or non-weight bearing assistance code limited assistance (2). If none of the above are met, code supervision

CodingInstructions: List each diagnosis for which the patient is receiving home care in Column 1, and enter its ICD-10-CM code at the level of highest specificity in Column 2 (diagnosis codes only - no surgical or procedure codes allowed). Diagnoses are listed in the order that best reflects the seriousness of each condition and supports the disciplines and services provided. Rate the degree of symptom control for each condition in Column 2. ICD-10-CM sequencing requirements must be followed if multiple coding is indicated for any diagnoses.   Code each row according to the following directions for each column:   Column 1: Enter the description of the diagnosis. Sequencing of diagnoses should reflect the seriousness of each condition and support the disciplines and services provided.   Column 2: Enter the ICD-10-CM code for the condition described in Column 1 - no surgical or procedure codes allowed. Codes must be entered at the level of highest specificity and ICD-10-CM coding rules and sequencing requirements must be followed. Note that external cause codes (ICD-10-CM codes beginning with V, W, X, or Y) may not be reported in M1021 (Primary Diagnosis) but may be reported in M1023 (Secondary Diagnoses). Also note that when a Z-code is reported in Column 2, the code for the underlying condition can often be entered in Column 2, as long as it is an active on-going condition impacting home health care.  Rate the degree of symptom control for the condition listed in Column 1. Do not assign a symptom control rating if the diagnosis code is a V, W, X, Y or Z-code. Choose one value that represents the degree of symptom control appropriate for each diagnosis using the following scale:  0 - Asymptomatic, no treatment needed at this time  1 - Symptoms well controlled with current therapy  2 - Symptoms controlled with difficulty, affecting daily functioning; patient needs ongoing monitoring  3 - Symptoms poorly controlled; patient needs frequent adjustment in treatment and dose monitoring  4 - Symptoms poorly controlled; history of re-hospitalizations  Note that the rating for symptom control in Column 2 should not be used to determine the sequencing of the diagnoses listed in Column 1. These are separate items and sequencing may not coincide

CodingInstructions: List each diagnosis for which the patient is receiving home care in Column 1, and enter its ICD-10-CM code at the level of highest specificity in Column 2 (diagnosis codes only - no surgical or procedure codes allowed). Diagnoses are listed in the order that best reflects the seriousness of each condition and supports the disciplines and services provided. Rate the degree of symptom control for each condition in Column 2. ICD-10-CM sequencing requirements must be followed if multiple coding is indicated for any diagnoses.   Code each row according to the following directions for each column:   Column 1: Enter the description of the diagnosis. Sequencing of diagnoses should reflect the seriousness of each condition and support the disciplines and services provided.   Column 2: Enter the ICD-10-CM code for the condition described in Column 1 - no surgical or procedure codes allowed. Codes must be entered at the level of highest specificity and ICD-10-CM coding rules and sequencing requirements must be followed. Note that external cause codes (ICD-10-CM codes beginning with V, W, X, or Y) may not be reported in M1021 (Primary Diagnosis) but may be reported in M1023 (Secondary Diagnoses). Also note that when a Z-code is reported in Column 2, the code for the underlying condition can often be entered in Column 2, as long as it is an active on-going condition impacting home health care.  Rate the degree of symptom control for the condition listed in Column 1. Do not assign a symptom control rating if the diagnosis code is a V, W, X, Y or Z-code. Choose one value that represents the degree of symptom control appropriate for each diagnosis using the following scale:  0 - Asymptomatic, no treatment needed at this time  1 - Symptoms well controlled with current therapy  2 - Symptoms controlled with difficulty, affecting daily functioning; patient needs ongoing monitoring  3 - Symptoms poorly controlled; patient needs frequent adjustment in treatment and dose monitoring  4 - Symptoms poorly controlled; history of re-hospitalizations  Note that the rating for symptom control in Column 2 should not be used to determine the sequencing of the diagnoses listed in Column 1. These are separate items and sequencing may not coincide

LoincName: OASIS E - Diagnoses and symptom control:-:RptPeriod:^Patient:-:CMS Assessment
CodingInstructions: List each diagnosis for which the patient is receiving home care in Column 1, and enter its ICD-10-CM code at the level of highest specificity in Column 2 (diagnosis codes only - no surgical or procedure codes allowed). Diagnoses are listed in the order that best reflects the seriousness of each condition and supports the disciplines and services provided. Rate the degree of symptom control for each condition in Column 2. ICD-10-CM sequencing requirements must be followed if multiple coding is indicated for any diagnoses.   Code each row according to the following directions for each column:   Column 1: Enter the description of the diagnosis. Sequencing of diagnoses should reflect the seriousness of each condition and support the disciplines and services provided.   Column 2: Enter the ICD-10-CM code for the condition described in Column 1 - no surgical or procedure codes allowed. Codes must be entered at the level of highest specificity and ICD-10-CM coding rules and sequencing requirements must be followed. Note that external cause codes (ICD-10-CM codes beginning with V, W, X, or Y) may not be reported in M1021 (Primary Diagnosis) but may be reported in M1023 (Secondary Diagnoses). Also note that when a Z-code is reported in Column 2, the code for the underlying condition can often be entered in Column 2, as long as it is an active on-going condition impacting home health care.  Rate the degree of symptom control for the condition listed in Column 1. Do not assign a symptom control rating if the diagnosis code is a V, W, X, Y or Z-code. Choose one value that represents the degree of symptom control appropriate for each diagnosis using the following scale:  0 - Asymptomatic, no treatment needed at this time  1 - Symptoms well controlled with current therapy  2 - Symptoms controlled with difficulty, affecting daily functioning; patient needs ongoing monitoring  3 - Symptoms poorly controlled; patient needs frequent adjustment in treatment and dose monitoring  4 - Symptoms poorly controlled; history of re-hospitalizations  Note that the rating for symptom control in Column 2 should not be used to determine the sequencing of the diagnoses listed in Column 1. These are separate items and sequencing may not coincide

CodingInstructions: Score of 0:   Vital signs (heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure) and/or oxygen saturations are within normal limits with normal variability or normal for gestational age. Score of -1:  Vital signs (heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure) show little variability with stimuli -- less than 10% from baseline Score of -2:  Any of the following: No variability in vital signs (heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure) with stimuli; Hypoventilation; Apnea; Ventilated infant no spontaneous respiratory effort noted by infant breathing over the ventilator.  (The measurement here is variability of the vital signs from the baseline.)

Score of 0:   Relaxed hands & feet; normal hand or foot grasp reflexes elicited; tone appropriate for gestational age Score of -1:  Any of the following:  Weak hand and foot grasp reflexes can be elicited; Decreased tone. Score of -2:  Any of the following:  No hand or foot grasp reflexes can be elicited; no tone noted

Score of 0:  Face is relaxed at rest but not lax -- appropriate gestational age facial movements  by observation of mouth and tensing of facial muscles with stimuli. Score of -1:  Minimal facial movements by observation of mouth and tensing of facial muscles with stimuli. Score of -2:  Any of the following: Mouth is lax (neutral position); Drooling; No facial movements by observation of mouth and tensing of facial muscles (no  at rest or with stimuli)

Score of 0:  Behavior and state are appropriate for gestational age. Score of -1:  Arouses minimally and/or intermittently to any stimuli; May open eyes briefly, Reacts to suctioning by pulling head back away from source; Minimal spontaneous movement of extremitites noted; Withdraws body part (i.e., head, hand, foot) from pain source when painful stimuli elicited. Score of -2:  No response to any stimuli; Eyes are either closed or open; No spontaneous movement of extremities; full sedation noted

Score of 0:  Not irritable;  appropriate crying for gestational age.  May cry intermittently with stimuli; consolable.    Score of -1:  Moans, sighs, or cries (audible, may have a silent cry if intubated - observed by the movements of mouth and tensing of facial muscles) minimally to painful stimuli, (e.g., needle sticks, ETT or nares suctioning, care giving).   Score of -2: No response by infant to painful stimuli; full sedation noted (e.g., No cry or silent cry with needle sticks; No reaction to ETT or nares suctioning; No response to care giving)

CodingInstructions: Score of 0:  Vital signs (heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure) and/or oxygen saturations are within normal limits with normal variability and/or appropriate for gestational age or clinical situation. Score of +1:  Any of the following: Heart rate, Respiratory Rate, and/or Blood Pressure are 10-20% above baseline vital signs; With care assessments and /or environmental stimuli infant oxygen saturations miniminally or moderately decreases (SpO2 76-85%) and then quickly returns to baseline oxygen saturation level (within 2 minutes).  Score of +2:  Any of the following: Heart Rate, Respiratory Rate, and/or Blood Pressure are >20% above baseline vital signs; With care assessments and/or environmental stimuli infant oxygen saturation level drops severely (SpO2 <75%) and then baseline oxygen saturation level recovers slowly (>2 minutes); Infant is breathing over the ventilator settings -- fighting the ventilator (The measurement here is variability of the vital signs from the baseline.)

Score of 0:  Relaxed hands & feet; hand or feet grasp reflexes and body tone appropriate for gestational age. Score of +1:  Intermittent (<30 seconds duration) observation of toes and/or hands as  clenched or fingers splayed; body is not tense. Score of +2:  Frequent (> or equal to 30 seconds duration) observation of toes and/or hands as clenched, or fingers splayed;  Body is tense (hypertonic)

Score of 0: Face is relaxed at rest; neutral position; with stimuli face muscles react appropriately for gestational age.  Score of +1: Any pain facial expression observed intermittently* (assessing intermittent tightening of muscles around the eyebrows, eyes, nose, chin, jaw, and mouth).  Score of +2: Any pain face expression is continual* (assessing continuous tightening of muscles around the eyebrows, eyes, nose, chin, jaw, and mouth). (*See Wong & Whaley drawing for pain face expressions)

Score of 0:  State and behavior are appropriate for gestational age. Score of +1:  Any of the following: Infant may be irritable; restless; easily awakens and frequently with minimal to no environmental stimuli (i.e, nurse interaction or noise). Score of +2:  Any of the following: Kicking of legs; Thrashing of extremities; Arching of neck and back; Constantly awake; Or No movement noted or minimal arousal with stimulation; lethargic; (however, not sedated, inappropriate for gestational age or clinical situation)

Score of 0:  Not irritable -- appropriate crying based on environmental stimuli (i.e, nurse interaction or noise) and gestational age; consolable. Score of +1: State of Irritability and crying at intervals; however still consolable; If intubated, will see intervals of silent crying (observed by the movements of mouth and tensing of facial muscles). Score of +2:  Any of the following: Cry is high-pitched; Infant cries inconsolably or in a disorganized state; If intubated - silent continuous crying (observed by the movements of mouth and tensing of facial muscles)

ParentName: OASIS E - Active Diagnoses - SOC:-:RptPeriod:^Patient:-:CMS Assessment
LoincName: OASIS E - Diagnoses and symptom control:-:RptPeriod:^Patient:-:CMS Assessment
CodingInstructions: List each diagnosis for which the patient is receiving home care in Column 1, and enter its ICD-10-CM code at the level of highest specificity in Column 2 (diagnosis codes only - no surgical or procedure codes allowed). Diagnoses are listed in the order that best reflects the seriousness of each condition and supports the disciplines and services provided. Rate the degree of symptom control for each condition in Column 2. ICD-10-CM sequencing requirements must be followed if multiple coding is indicated for any diagnoses.   Code each row according to the following directions for each column:   Column 1: Enter the description of the diagnosis. Sequencing of diagnoses should reflect the seriousness of each condition and support the disciplines and services provided.   Column 2: Enter the ICD-10-CM code for the condition described in Column 1 - no surgical or procedure codes allowed. Codes must be entered at the level of highest specificity and ICD-10-CM coding rules and sequencing requirements must be followed. Note that external cause codes (ICD-10-CM codes beginning with V, W, X, or Y) may not be reported in M1021 (Primary Diagnosis) but may be reported in M1023 (Secondary Diagnoses). Also note that when a Z-code is reported in Column 2, the code for the underlying condition can often be entered in Column 2, as long as it is an active on-going condition impacting home health care.  Rate the degree of symptom control for the condition listed in Column 1. Do not assign a symptom control rating if the diagnosis code is a V, W, X, Y or Z-code. Choose one value that represents the degree of symptom control appropriate for each diagnosis using the following scale:  0 - Asymptomatic, no treatment needed at this time  1 - Symptoms well controlled with current therapy  2 - Symptoms controlled with difficulty, affecting daily functioning; patient needs ongoing monitoring  3 - Symptoms poorly controlled; patient needs frequent adjustment in treatment and dose monitoring  4 - Symptoms poorly controlled; history of re-hospitalizations  Note that the rating for symptom control in Column 2 should not be used to determine the sequencing of the diagnoses listed in Column 1. These are separate items and sequencing may not coincide

LoincName: OASIS E - Diagnoses and symptom control:-:RptPeriod:^Patient:-:CMS Assessment
CodingInstructions: List each diagnosis for which the patient is receiving home care in Column 1, and enter its ICD-10-CM code at the level of highest specificity in Column 2 (diagnosis codes only - no surgical or procedure codes allowed). Diagnoses are listed in the order that best reflects the seriousness of each condition and supports the disciplines and services provided. Rate the degree of symptom control for each condition in Column 2. ICD-10-CM sequencing requirements must be followed if multiple coding is indicated for any diagnoses.   Code each row according to the following directions for each column:   Column 1: Enter the description of the diagnosis. Sequencing of diagnoses should reflect the seriousness of each condition and support the disciplines and services provided.   Column 2: Enter the ICD-10-CM code for the condition described in Column 1 - no surgical or procedure codes allowed. Codes must be entered at the level of highest specificity and ICD-10-CM coding rules and sequencing requirements must be followed. Note that external cause codes (ICD-10-CM codes beginning with V, W, X, or Y) may not be reported in M1021 (Primary Diagnosis) but may be reported in M1023 (Secondary Diagnoses). Also note that when a Z-code is reported in Column 2, the code for the underlying condition can often be entered in Column 2, as long as it is an active on-going condition impacting home health care.  Rate the degree of symptom control for the condition listed in Column 1. Do not assign a symptom control rating if the diagnosis code is a V, W, X, Y or Z-code. Choose one value that represents the degree of symptom control appropriate for each diagnosis using the following scale:  0 - Asymptomatic, no treatment needed at this time  1 - Symptoms well controlled with current therapy  2 - Symptoms controlled with difficulty, affecting daily functioning; patient needs ongoing monitoring  3 - Symptoms poorly controlled; patient needs frequent adjustment in treatment and dose monitoring  4 - Symptoms poorly controlled; history of re-hospitalizations  Note that the rating for symptom control in Column 2 should not be used to determine the sequencing of the diagnoses listed in Column 1. These are separate items and sequencing may not coincide

CodingInstructions: Instructions: Based on your assessment, please answer the following questions about the individual's spoken language expression skills in low and high demand communication exchanges. For all questions, consider chronological age expectations when rating the individual. • Low demand situations are defined as interactive situations where communication demands are reduced (e.g., shorter messages, familiar setting, familiar conversation partner, known context). For children this may also include verbal messages in conversation or activities that primarily require language, content and forms acquired at a younger age than the child's current age. • High demand situations are defined as interactive situations that provide minimal support and have inherently more communication demands or rules to follow (e.g., longer messages, unfamiliar conversational partner or setting, unknown contexts, group conversations/activities). For children this may also include verbal messages requiring language, content and forms that are more recently acquired or expected for the child's current age. Please note that the scale is reversed for the first question only. For example, a score of 0-25% indicates the highest functioning for the first question only. Note: This scale should be used for individuals with verbal expression treatment goals. If you are also working on other aspects of expressive language (e.g., gestures, AAC), consider scoring the individual on the Multi-Modal Functional Communication scale as well

CodingInstructions: Critical aspects: Different painful areas which are felt by the patient to belong together as one pain are coded with a "1"; e.g. back pain and leg pain occurring together and felt as one pain. CodingInstructions: Pain-related drugs are grouped in the following manner for comparison's sake: Group I: Non-opioid analgesics (mono-substances, e.g. NSAIDS, paracetamol, metamizol); Group II: weak and strong opioids; Group III: fixed-ratio-combination drugs, e.g. migraine drugs, muscle relaxants, tranquilizer, antidepressants, neuroleptics, anti- convulsants, corticosteroidsetc, as long as they are used as analgesics or co-analgesics

DisplayNameForForm: I tried not to talk about it.

DisplayNameForForm: Reminders of it caused me to have physical reactions, such as sweating, trouble breathing, nausea, or a pounding heart.

LoincName: Tried to remove adverse event from memory:Find:RptPeriod:^Patient:Ord:
DisplayNameForForm: I tried to remove it from my memory.

LoincName: Waves of strong feelings about adverse event:Find:RptPeriod:^Patient:Ord:
DisplayNameForForm: I had waves of strong feelings about it.

DisplayNameForForm: I found myslef acting or feeling like I was back at that time.

LoincName: Feelings about adverse event were numb:Find:RptPeriod:^Patient:Ord:
DisplayNameForForm: My feelings about it were kind of numb.

DisplayNameForForm: I was aware that I still had a lot of feelings about it, but I didn't deal with them.

DisplayNameForForm: I tried not to think about it.
I was jumpy and easily startled.

LoincName: Experienced mental images of adverse event:Find:RptPeriod:^Patient:Ord:
DisplayNameForForm: Pictures about it popped into my mind.
I stayed away from reminders of it.

LoincName: Felt as if adverse event did not happen:Find:RptPeriod:^Patient:Ord:
DisplayNameForForm: I felt as if it hadn't happened or wasn't real.
I thought about it when I didn't mean to.

LoincName: Avoided getting upset when unintentionally thought about adverse event:Find:RptPeriod:^Patient:Ord:
DisplayNameForForm: I avoided letting myself get upset when I thought about it or was reminded of it.

LoincName: Other things triggered persistent thoughts about adverse event:Find:RptPeriod:^Patient:Ord:
DisplayNameForForm: Other things kept making me think about it.
When I'm walking, I deliberately notice the sensations of my body moving.

I notice the smells and aromas of things.

CodingInstructions: 1. Smiling or inexpressive. Smiling is characterized by upturned corners of the mouth, brightening of the eyes, and a look of pleasure or contentment. Inexpressive refers to a neutral, at ease, relaxed, or blank look. 2. Sad is characterized by an unhappy, lonesome, sorrowful, or dejected look. There may be tears in the eyes. 3. Frightened is characterized by a look of fear, alarm, or heightened anxiety. Eyes appear wide open. 4. Frown is characterized by a downward turn of the corners of the mouth. Increased facial wrinkling in the forehead and around the mouth may appear. 5. Facial grimacing is characterized by a distorted, distressed look. The brow is more wrinkled, as is the area around the mouth. Eyes may be squeezed shut.

ParentName: IRF-PAI v4.0, LCDS v5.00, OASIS E - Mood:-:RptPeriod:^Patient:-:CMS Assessment
DisplayNameForForm: Patient Mood Interview (PHQ-2 to 9) (from Pfizer Inc.©)
CodingInstructions: Determine if the patient is rarely/never understood verbally, in writing, or using another method. If rarely/never understood, code D0150A1 and D0150B1 as 9, No response, leave D0150A2 and D0150B2 blank, end the PHQ-2 interview, and leave D0160, Total Severity Score blank. Otherwise, say to patient: "Over the last 2 weeks, have you been bothered by any of the following problems?" If symptom is present, enter 1 (yes) in column 1, Symptom Presence. If yes in column 1, then ask the patient: "About how often have you been bothered by this?" Read and show the patient a card with the symptom frequency choices. Indicate response in column 2, Symptom Frequency

If yes in column 1, then ask the patient: "About how often have you been bothered by this?" Read and show the patient a card with the symptom frequency choices. Indicate response in column 2, Symptom Frequency

ParentName: OASIS E - Active Diagnoses - SOC:-:RptPeriod:^Patient:-:CMS Assessment
LoincName: OASIS E - Diagnoses and symptom control:-:RptPeriod:^Patient:-:CMS Assessment
CodingInstructions: List each diagnosis for which the patient is receiving home care in Column 1, and enter its ICD-10-CM code at the level of highest specificity in Column 2 (diagnosis codes only - no surgical or procedure codes allowed). Diagnoses are listed in the order that best reflects the seriousness of each condition and supports the disciplines and services provided. Rate the degree of symptom control for each condition in Column 2. ICD-10-CM sequencing requirements must be followed if multiple coding is indicated for any diagnoses.   Code each row according to the following directions for each column:   Column 1: Enter the description of the diagnosis. Sequencing of diagnoses should reflect the seriousness of each condition and support the disciplines and services provided.   Column 2: Enter the ICD-10-CM code for the condition described in Column 1 - no surgical or procedure codes allowed. Codes must be entered at the level of highest specificity and ICD-10-CM coding rules and sequencing requirements must be followed. Note that external cause codes (ICD-10-CM codes beginning with V, W, X, or Y) may not be reported in M1021 (Primary Diagnosis) but may be reported in M1023 (Secondary Diagnoses). Also note that when a Z-code is reported in Column 2, the code for the underlying condition can often be entered in Column 2, as long as it is an active on-going condition impacting home health care.  Rate the degree of symptom control for the condition listed in Column 1. Do not assign a symptom control rating if the diagnosis code is a V, W, X, Y or Z-code. Choose one value that represents the degree of symptom control appropriate for each diagnosis using the following scale:  0 - Asymptomatic, no treatment needed at this time  1 - Symptoms well controlled with current therapy  2 - Symptoms controlled with difficulty, affecting daily functioning; patient needs ongoing monitoring  3 - Symptoms poorly controlled; patient needs frequent adjustment in treatment and dose monitoring  4 - Symptoms poorly controlled; history of re-hospitalizations  Note that the rating for symptom control in Column 2 should not be used to determine the sequencing of the diagnoses listed in Column 1. These are separate items and sequencing may not coincide

LoincName: OASIS E - Diagnoses and symptom control:-:RptPeriod:^Patient:-:CMS Assessment
CodingInstructions: List each diagnosis for which the patient is receiving home care in Column 1, and enter its ICD-10-CM code at the level of highest specificity in Column 2 (diagnosis codes only - no surgical or procedure codes allowed). Diagnoses are listed in the order that best reflects the seriousness of each condition and supports the disciplines and services provided. Rate the degree of symptom control for each condition in Column 2. ICD-10-CM sequencing requirements must be followed if multiple coding is indicated for any diagnoses.   Code each row according to the following directions for each column:   Column 1: Enter the description of the diagnosis. Sequencing of diagnoses should reflect the seriousness of each condition and support the disciplines and services provided.   Column 2: Enter the ICD-10-CM code for the condition described in Column 1 - no surgical or procedure codes allowed. Codes must be entered at the level of highest specificity and ICD-10-CM coding rules and sequencing requirements must be followed. Note that external cause codes (ICD-10-CM codes beginning with V, W, X, or Y) may not be reported in M1021 (Primary Diagnosis) but may be reported in M1023 (Secondary Diagnoses). Also note that when a Z-code is reported in Column 2, the code for the underlying condition can often be entered in Column 2, as long as it is an active on-going condition impacting home health care.  Rate the degree of symptom control for the condition listed in Column 1. Do not assign a symptom control rating if the diagnosis code is a V, W, X, Y or Z-code. Choose one value that represents the degree of symptom control appropriate for each diagnosis using the following scale:  0 - Asymptomatic, no treatment needed at this time  1 - Symptoms well controlled with current therapy  2 - Symptoms controlled with difficulty, affecting daily functioning; patient needs ongoing monitoring  3 - Symptoms poorly controlled; patient needs frequent adjustment in treatment and dose monitoring  4 - Symptoms poorly controlled; history of re-hospitalizations  Note that the rating for symptom control in Column 2 should not be used to determine the sequencing of the diagnoses listed in Column 1. These are separate items and sequencing may not coincide

DisplayNameForForm: Frequency of Disruptive Behavior Symptoms (reported or observed): Any physical, verbal, or other disruptive/dangerous symptoms that are injurious to self or others or jeopardize personal safety.
Grooming: Current ability to tend safely to personal hygiene needs (specifically: washing face and hands, hair care, shaving or make up, teeth or denture care, or fingernail care).

LoincName: Dress lower body - functional ability:Find:RptPeriod:^Patient:Ord:CMS Assessment
DisplayNameForForm: Current Ability to Dress Lower Body safely (with or without dressing aids) including undergarments, slacks, socks or nylons, shoes.
Bathing: Current ability to wash entire body safely. Excludes grooming (washing face, washing hands, and shampooing hair).
Toilet Transferring: Current ability to get to and from the toilet or bedside commode safely and transfer on and off toilet/commode.

Toileting Hygiene: Current ability to maintain perineal hygiene safely, adjust clothes and/or incontinence pads before and after using toilet, commode, bedpan, urinal. If managing ostomy, includes cleaning area around stoma, but not managing equipment.
Transferring: Current ability to move safely from bed to chair, or ability to turn and position self in bed if patient is bedfast.
Ambulation/Locomotion: Current ability to walk safely, once in a standing position, or use a wheelchair, once in a seated position, on a variety of surfaces.

LoincName: OASIS E - Diagnoses and symptom control:-:RptPeriod:^Patient:-:CMS Assessment
CodingInstructions: List each diagnosis for which the patient is receiving home care in Column 1, and enter its ICD-10-CM code at the level of highest specificity in Column 2 (diagnosis codes only - no surgical or procedure codes allowed). Diagnoses are listed in the order that best reflects the seriousness of each condition and supports the disciplines and services provided. Rate the degree of symptom control for each condition in Column 2. ICD-10-CM sequencing requirements must be followed if multiple coding is indicated for any diagnoses.   Code each row according to the following directions for each column:   Column 1: Enter the description of the diagnosis. Sequencing of diagnoses should reflect the seriousness of each condition and support the disciplines and services provided.   Column 2: Enter the ICD-10-CM code for the condition described in Column 1 - no surgical or procedure codes allowed. Codes must be entered at the level of highest specificity and ICD-10-CM coding rules and sequencing requirements must be followed. Note that external cause codes (ICD-10-CM codes beginning with V, W, X, or Y) may not be reported in M1021 (Primary Diagnosis) but may be reported in M1023 (Secondary Diagnoses). Also note that when a Z-code is reported in Column 2, the code for the underlying condition can often be entered in Column 2, as long as it is an active on-going condition impacting home health care.  Rate the degree of symptom control for the condition listed in Column 1. Do not assign a symptom control rating if the diagnosis code is a V, W, X, Y or Z-code. Choose one value that represents the degree of symptom control appropriate for each diagnosis using the following scale:  0 - Asymptomatic, no treatment needed at this time  1 - Symptoms well controlled with current therapy  2 - Symptoms controlled with difficulty, affecting daily functioning; patient needs ongoing monitoring  3 - Symptoms poorly controlled; patient needs frequent adjustment in treatment and dose monitoring  4 - Symptoms poorly controlled; history of re-hospitalizations  Note that the rating for symptom control in Column 2 should not be used to determine the sequencing of the diagnoses listed in Column 1. These are separate items and sequencing may not coincide
